en.title: Hobbies and free time
en.goal: Talk about hobbies, likes and what you do in your free time.

lessons.hobbies-leitura: Talking about hobbies: reading and listening to music

vocab: to be free / have free time

phrases.t: I like reading books and listening to music.

dialogue.title: Making plans
lines: I like watching movies and dancing. And you?
I like to exercise. Are you free this weekend?
I am! Let's go see a movie.

de-posse.title: 的 (de) — showing possession
de-posse.body: 的 (de) is used to show possession, like "my", "your", "someone's" — similar to the English "'s", but simpler: it always goes between the owner and the thing owned. The structure is: Owner + 的 + Thing.

kan-vs-ting.title: "Kàn" or "tīng"?
kan-vs-ting.body: Kàn (看) is used for visual activities: reading, watching a movie. Tīng (听) is used for listening activities. Mixing the two up is a common mistake — "listening to a movie" or "watching music" sounds odd in Chinese, just as it would in English.

guangchangwu-danca-praca.title: Square dancing: a very Chinese hobby
guangchangwu-danca-praca.body: In squares and parks all over China, it's common to see groups — usually middle-aged and older women — gathering every late afternoon to dance together to music, in a tradition known as guǎngchǎng wǔ (广场舞, "square dance"). It is both physical exercise and an important social moment for that generation.

trueFalse.claim: This is a way of inviting someone to do something.
trueFalse.whyNote: Correct — 你有空吗？ asks whether the person is free/available, a common way to invite someone to do something on the weekend.
